learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze grouped data sets by calculating their Mean, Median, and Mode, and understand how to extract meaning from large sets of information!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The average. Two main methods to find it: 1. Direct Method [Σ(fi × xi) / Σfi]. 2. Assumed Mean Method [a + Σ(fi × di) / Σfi]. 'xi' represents the class mark (midpoint of the interval).
The value that occurs most frequently. First, locate the 'Modal Class' (class with highest frequency). Then apply the formula: l + [(f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2)] × h.
The middle value. You must calculate the Cumulative Frequency (cf) first. Locate the 'Median Class' (where cf is just greater than n/2). Apply formula: l + [(n/2 - cf) / f] × h.
There is a direct mathematical connection between all three central tendencies: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean. This is highly useful for 1-mark questions.

fun_activity.title: 👟 The Shoe Size Survey
fun_activity.instructions: Ask 10 of your friends or family members for their shoe sizes. Which size appears the most? That's your 'Mode'! Add them all up and divide by 10 to find the 'Mean'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always check if class intervals are continuous (e.g., 10-20, 20-30). If they are discontinuous (10-19, 20-29), subtract 0.5 from the lower limit and add 0.5 to the upper limit before calculating.
📌 Creating neat, well-ruled columns in your answer sheet prevents silly addition mistakes in statistics.
📌 In the Median formula, 'cf' is the cumulative frequency of the class PRECEDING (just before) the median class, not the median class itself.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Class Mark (xi) is found by: (Upper Limit + Lower Limit) / 2.
⭐ Mean is best for data without extreme outliers. Median is best when extreme outliers exist.
⭐ In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, Mean = Median = Mode.
